# Spice v2.2.0-rc.1 (September 2, 2026)

Spice v2.2.0-rc.1 is the first release candidate for v2.2.0. Spice Cayenne adds a bounded scan concurrency setting. The MongoDB connector reads change streams for `refresh_mode: changes`.

Highlights in this release candidate include:

- **[Bounded Cayenne Scan Concurrency](#bounded-cayenne-scan-concurrency)** — the new `cayenne_scan_concurrency` setting holds peak resident memory within the query memory limit
- **[MongoDB Change Streams](#mongodb-change-streams)** — MongoDB collections replicate through `refresh_mode: changes`

## What's New in v2.2.0-rc.1

### Bounded Cayenne Scan Concurrency

The new `cayenne_scan_concurrency` setting bounds how many Vortex files [Spice Cayenne](https://spiceai.org/docs/components/data-accelerators/cayenne) decodes at once. The default value `auto` derives the bound from the CPU budget. An integer pins it.

```yaml
acceleration:
  engine: cayenne
  params:
    cayenne_scan_concurrency: auto # 'auto' (default) or an integer
```

On a 96-core node with a 4-core entitlement, the previous code opened one decode task for each file group. Peak resident memory reached 3.2 times the query memory limit on TPC-DS q64. The bound holds peak resident memory within the limit. Scan throughput is unchanged on the SF-100 benchmark.

### MongoDB Change Streams

The [MongoDB](https://spiceai.org/docs/components/data-connectors/mongodb) data connector supports `refresh_mode: changes`. It reads a collection change stream and applies inserts, updates, and deletes to the acceleration. A resume token is checkpointed with each batch, so a restart continues from the last applied change.

```yaml
datasets:
  - from: mongodb:sales.orders
    name: orders
    acceleration:
      engine: cayenne
      refresh_mode: changes
```

## Upgrading

To upgrade to v2.2.0-rc.1, use one of the following methods:

**CLI**:

```console
spice upgrade
```

**Homebrew**:

```console
brew upgrade spiceai/spiceai/spice
```

**Docker**:

Pull the `spiceai/spiceai:2.2.0-rc.1` image:

```console
docker pull spiceai/spiceai:2.2.0-rc.1
```

For available tags, see [DockerHub](https://hub.docker.com/r/spiceai/spiceai/tags).
